payload.title: Aurora-Borealis Supply Agreement - 10-Round Three-Seat Negotiation
payload.description: Aurora Corp is ramping Line-7 (a new product line) and needs 5,000 precision actuators delivered before a fixed retooling window starting Day 35. Borealis Components is a qualified supplier with a Q3 capacity gap and quarterly bookings target. Both sides have meaningful BATNAs (alternate supplier vs. wholesale offload) but both BATNAs leave value on the table relative to a deal in the $44-$48 range. The negotiation tests price anchoring, log-rolling (warranty <-> price, prepayment <-> delivery), and use of a non-binding follow-on framework as a sweetener.

scenario.title: Aurora vs Borealis — 5,000-unit Supply Negotiation
scenario.shortDescription: Mid-sized OEM (Aurora) negotiating a one-time 5,000-unit precision-actuator order with mid-tier supplier (Borealis); ZOPA exists between $44–$48/unit but each side is anchoring outside it.
scenario.context: Aurora Corp is ramping Line-7 (a new product line) and needs 5,000 precision actuators delivered before a fixed retooling window starting Day 35. Borealis Components is a qualified supplier with a Q3 capacity gap and quarterly bookings target. Both sides have meaningful BATNAs (alternate supplier vs. wholesale offload) but both BATNAs leave value on the table relative to a deal in the $44–$48 range. The negotiation tests price anchoring, log-rolling (warranty <-> price, prepayment <-> delivery), and use of a non-binding follow-on framework as a sweetener.

history.label: Borealis qualified as Tier-1 supplier
history.detail: Aurora Procurement completed quality and audit qualification of Borealis after a 90-day review.

history.label: Aurora's prior vendor missed delivery
history.detail: Previous actuator vendor missed delivery on a 2,000-unit order, costing Aurora ~$180k in line-stop time. CFO approved switch to a more reliable supplier even at modest price premium.

recentEvents.label: Borealis posts Q3 capacity availability
recentEvents.detail: Borealis CRO flags 78% capacity utilization and a $2.1M bookings gap; sales team aggressive on closing Q3 deals.

recentEvents.label: RFQ issued
recentEvents.detail: Aurora issued formal RFQ to Borealis with $42 target, 30-day delivery, 24-month warranty, 25% prepay cap.

pastAgreements.label: NDA + supplier code-of-conduct
pastAgreements.detail: Mutual NDA and supplier code signed; no prior commercial volume.

impacts.summary: If deal lands at <=$42, Q3 cost-reduction mandate hits target; if walks to BATNA, hits target but burns 60h of QA on supplier re-qualification and adds 5-day delivery risk to Line-7.
If deal lands at >=$48 with 40% prepay, closes the $2.1M Q3 gap and amortizes tooling; if walks to BATNA (wholesale), revenue lands but margin drops to 16% and Q4 inventory is still exposed.

personas.role: Buyer-side Director of Strategic Procurement at Aurora Corp, mid-sized industrial OEM under Q3 cost-reduction mandate from CFO; reports to VP Operations.
personas.systemPromptOverride: You represent Aurora Corp, a buyer of 5,000 precision actuator units. You have a cost-reduction mandate but value supplier reliability — Aurora's last vendor missed delivery and triggered a $180k production stoppage. Open with anchoring, but be willing to trade pre-payment for faster delivery, or warranty length for price.

goals.description: Secure a per-unit price at or below $42 for the 5,000-unit order (target spend $210k vs. $230k BATNA = 9% savings to land Q3 mandate).
Delivery completed within 30 days of contract signature to align with Aurora's Line-7 retooling window starting Day 35.
Obtain a 24-month warranty with on-site replacement (CFO requires >=18 months for capitalization treatment).
Cap pre-payment exposure to protect working-capital line; would prefer 15% upfront, 35% on shipment, 50% net-30.
Plant a seed for a 3-year master supply agreement once trust is established (volume forecast ~12k units/yr).

redLines.description: Will not accept any per-unit price above $48 — board-approved ceiling tied to BATNA + 4% switching cost.
Will not pre-pay more than 25% before delivery — Treasury policy on counterparty exposure for non-rated suppliers.
Will not accept delivery later than Day 45 — Line-7 retooling slot is non-cancellable.

batna.description: Walk away and award the contract to Supplier-X (Tier-2 vendor in Mexico, qualified Q1) at $46/unit with 35-day delivery and 18-month warranty. Adds 5-day buffer to Line-7 schedule and burns 60h of QA re-qualification time. Total landed cost: $230k + ~$18k re-qualification = $248k.

tactics.name: Anchor low on opening
tactics.description: Open round 1 with $35/unit citing internal cost build-up; sets the negotiation frame and protects the $42 target.

tactics.name: Reveal BATNA pressure (oblique)
tactics.description: When stalled 2+ rounds, mention 'we have alternative suppliers under evaluation' without naming Supplier-X; signals walk-away credibility without burning the relationship.

tactics.name: Log-roll warranty for price
tactics.description: When seller anchors high, offer to drop the 24-month warranty ask to 18 months in exchange for a $3/unit price reduction.

tactics.name: Trade pre-payment for delivery
tactics.description: If seller pushes >35% pre-pay, offer 30% pre-pay only if they guarantee Day-25 delivery with liquidated damages.

tactics.name: Dangle 3-year master agreement
tactics.description: Round 3+: float the possibility of a 3-year MSA to extract concession on this order; non-binding LOI.
